nodes.name: Chat Webhook
nodes.notes: POST /webhook/chat/message. responseMode is "responseNode", not "onReceived": the visitor gets the actual answer in the body of this same request, which is what "replies immediately" has to mean for a chat widget. allowedOrigins is * for the demo; set it to the client's own domain in production - docs/setup.md says how and why.

nodes.name: Verify Shared Secret
nodes.notes: Authenticates, validates and normalises before anything is written or spent. The money sweep is the same list as workflow 01, deliberately: the gate must behave identically whichever door the question came through.

parameters.query:
-- One row per widget session. ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE rather than a prior SELECT,
-- because a visitor who types two messages quickly can have two executions in
-- flight and both would find no session and both would insert.
--
-- visitor_email uses coalesce(excluded, existing): a visitor who gives their
-- address on message four must not have it erased by message five, which sends
-- nothing.
INSERT INTO chat_sessions (session_id, visitor_email, first_page_url)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3)
ON CONFLICT (session_id) DO UPDATE
   SET last_seen_at  = now(),
       visitor_email = coalesce(excluded.visitor_email, chat_sessions.visitor_email)
RETURNING session_id, started_at;

-- The memory. Without this every message is the visitor's first, and the agent
-- answers "what about annual?" as if it had never heard of a plan.
--
-- Ordered DESC in the subquery to take the LAST n, then ASC on the way out so
-- the model reads the conversation forwards.
SELECT * FROM (
  SELECT role, content, created_at
    FROM chat_messages
   WHERE session_id = $1
   ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC
   LIMIT $2::int
) AS recent
ORDER BY created_at ASC;

nodes.name: Load Recent Turns
nodes.notes: alwaysOutputData so the first message of a session - which has no history - still emits an item.

nodes.name: Ask The Answer Engine
nodes.notes: The same workflow 03 the Gmail agent calls - the same n8n workflow id, not a copy. That is what "connected to the same backend" means here: add an article, change the prompt or move the relevance floor once and both channels change together.

nodes.name: Confidence Gate
nodes.notes: The same four conditions as workflow 01, reading the same env var. A refund question typed into the chat widget gets a human for exactly the same reason one sent by email does.

nodes.name: Compose Handover Reply
nodes.notes: Says "I do not know" in one sentence and hands over. Every extra sentence a bot writes when it has nothing to say is a sentence the customer has to read before they find out they are still stuck.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ session_id: $json.session_id, reply: $json.reply_text, grounded: $json.grounded, handed_to_human: $json.needs_human, used_article_ids: $json.used_article_ids, answered_at: new Date().toISOString() }) }}

nodes.name: Respond To Visitor
nodes.notes: The visitor gets their answer here, in the response to their own POST - no polling, no second connection, no "we will email you". Everything after this node is bookkeeping, and it runs after the browser already has the reply.

parameters.query:
-- The same table workflow 01 writes to, with channel = 'chat'. One log for the
-- whole desk means one query answers "what did support do today", whichever
-- door the question came through.
INSERT INTO support_decisions
  (decision_key, channel, from_address, subject, conversation_ref, intent, is_support,
   confidence, grounded, touches_money, action, inbound_text, reply_text,
   used_article_ids, reason, integration_error, execution_id)
VALUES ($1, 'chat', $2, $3, $4, 'chat_message', true, $5, $6, $7, $8, $9, $10, $11::bigint[], $12, $13, $14)
ON CONFLICT (decision_key) DO UPDATE
   SET action            = excluded.action,
       confidence        = excluded.confidence,
       grounded          = excluded.grounded,
       reply_text        = excluded.reply_text,
       used_article_ids  = excluded.used_article_ids,
       reason            = excluded.reason,
       integration_error = excluded.integration_error,
       execution_id      = excluded.execution_id
RETURNING id, action;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ (() => { const c = $('Reply Ready').first().json; return [c.decision_key, c.visitor_email, (c.message || "").slice(0, 120), c.session_id, c.confidence, c.grounded, c.touches_money, c.action, c.message, c.reply_text, "{" + (c.used_article_ids || []).join(",") + "}", c.handover_reason || "answered from articles " + (c.used_article_ids || []).join(", "), c.integration_error, String($execution.id)]; })() }}

parameters.query:
-- The visitor's message and the agent's reply, in that order, in one
-- statement. Two separate INSERTs would leave a window where a crash records
-- the question and not the answer, and the next message in the session would
-- then be answered against a transcript that lies.
INSERT INTO chat_messages (session_id, role, content, grounded)
VALUES ($1, 'visitor', $2, NULL),
       ($1, 'agent',   $3, $4)
RETURNING id, role;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ (() => { const c = $('Reply Ready').first().json; return [c.session_id, c.message, c.reply_text, c.grounded]; })() }}

nodes.name: Persist Both Turns
nodes.notes: This is what makes the next message in the session answerable in the light of this one. Written after the response has already gone out, so the visitor never waits on it.

nodes.name: Needs A Human?
nodes.notes: Runs after the visitor has their reply. Queueing and alerting are not on the visitor's critical path and should never be.

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO human_review_queue
  (decision_key, channel, conversation_ref, from_address, subject, question, reason, confidence, suggested_answer)
VALUES ($1, 'chat', $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7, $8)
ON CONFLICT (decision_key) DO NOTHING
RETURNING id, created_at;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ (() => { const c = $('Reply Ready').first().json; return [c.decision_key, c.session_id, c.visitor_email, 'Live chat - ' + (c.page_url || 'unknown page'), c.message, c.handover_reason, c.confidence, c.answer]; })() }}

nodes.name: Queue For A Human
nodes.notes: Unique on decision_key: a visitor who impatiently sends the same sentence twice opens one ticket, not two.

nodes.name: Alert The Review Channel
nodes.notes: Both outputs land on the same recorder below: the ticket is already in the queue whether or not Slack took the message, and the log has to say which.

parameters.query:
-- The alert either landed or it did not, and the decision row says so. A
-- failures table that only contains the failures you were successfully told
-- about is not a failures table.
UPDATE support_decisions
   SET integration_error = $2
 WHERE decision_key = $1
   AND $2 IS NOT NULL
RETURNING id, integration_error;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [ $('Reply Ready').first().json.decision_key, $json.error ? 'Alert The Review Channel - ' + String($json.error.message || 'failed').slice(0, 200) : null ] }}

nodes.name: Record Alert Outcome
nodes.notes: Updates nothing on the happy path, which is why alwaysOutputData is on.

nodes.name: Answered Without A Human
nodes.notes: The branch that needed nobody. Kept as a node rather than left dangling so the canvas shows the good path ending deliberately.
